Alleging that a huge stock of scented tobacco was found in possession of the applicant during the raid effected on 28.10.2018 stocked in his godown the applicant was accosted.
A report was lodged.
The articles were seized.

The crime was registered for the offences punishable under Section 188, 272, 273, 328 read with Section 34 of the I.P.C. and also for the offences punishable under Section 23, 26(2),
27, 30(2)(a) and 59(iv) of the Food Safety and Standard Act.
The applicant was arrested on the same day and is now seeking bail after filing of the charge-sheet.

3. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application.
4. Perusal of the charge-sheet reveals that the investigation has already been over.

As is pointed out by the learned advocate for the applicant, except the offence punishable under Section 328 of the I.P.C.
the rest of the offences are bailable and do not attract severe punishment.

5. As far as Section 328 of the I.P.C. is concerned accepting the allegations of the prosecution at its face value, it is not its case about the applicant having administered or caused to administer alleged stupefying substance to anybody.
It is under these circumstances, in my considered view the applicant deserves to be released on bail.

Hence I pass the following order:
 ORDER  I) The application is allowed.

3 20 ba 30.19.odt III) Bail before the lower Court.
IV) It is made clear that the observations made herein-above are only prima facie and confined to the decision of this application and the trial Judge shall not feel influenced by them.
